    Interlaced paths and contours #

    Two paths are interlaced if they are linked by steps p v' q ~ p w' q with v' = w' ≠ 0 and p, q not both trivial (Gabriel–Roiter 13.6); a contour is a pair of non-interlaced paths with the same nonzero value. If a morphism μ occurs in no contour, the homotopy relation with the pairs of value μ removed (homotopyExcept μ) has the same quotient as the full homotopy relation, so the fundamental groups agree (RayCat.endEquivExcept). With P/μ this is part (b) of the lemma in Section 3.1 of Bongartz, Indecomposables live in all smaller lengths.
